research_metadata.topic: Popular coding workflows, coding style/structure documentation practices, and developer workflow repositories

section_1_ai_instruction_files.title: AI Agent Instruction Files (Emerging Standard)
section_1_ai_instruction_files.summary: The pattern of providing AI coding agents with project-specific instruction files has become a major trend in 2025-2026. Three major formats have emerged: CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules/.cursor/rules, and .github/copilot-instructions.md. A unification effort (amplified.dev, aicodingrules.org) is underway.

claude_md.description: Special file read by Claude Code at start of every conversation. Provides persistent context about project conventions.
recommended_sections: Project context/overview (1-liner about what the project is)
Code style guidelines (formatting, conventions differing from defaults)
what_to_include: Code style rules that differ from defaults
Testing instructions and preferred test runners
Architectural decisions specific to your project
what_to_exclude: Anything Claude can figure out by reading code
Standard language conventions Claude already knows
Detailed API documentation (link to docs instead)
claude_md.size_guidelines: Under 150-300 lines. Shorter is better. Every line should answer: 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?'

advanced_features.skills: .claude/skills/ directories with SKILL.md for on-demand knowledge
advanced_features.subagents: .claude/agents/ for specialized assistants with isolated context
advanced_features.hooks: Deterministic scripts at lifecycle events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.)

example_repos.name: shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice
example_repos.notes: Example CLAUDE.md with Weather System, Skill Definitions, Hooks. Recommends <150 lines.

example_repos.name: ChrisWiles/claude-code-showcase
example_repos.notes: Comprehensive .claude/ directory: hooks, skills, agents, commands, GitHub Actions.

example_repos.name: ArthurClune/claude-md-examples
example_repos.notes: Collection of CLAUDE.md examples for different project types.

cursorrules.description: Configuration files (.cursorrules or .cursor/rules/*.mdc) that enhance Cursor AI editor with custom rules and behaviors.
cursorrules.format: Markdown with YAML frontmatter (description, globs, alwaysApply)
recommended_content: Planning and context instructions (understand system before coding)
Code quality standards (bullet plan before execution, no unnecessary logic)
Error handling conventions (guard clauses, early returns)
key_patterns: Use .cursor/*.mdc files for composable rules (reduces token usage)
Give rules concrete names and descriptions
Be specific and actionable, not vague
Legacy .cursorrules still supported but deprecated in favor of .cursor/rules/
popular_categories: Frontend: React, Vue, Next.js, Angular, Svelte, Astro
Backend: Node.js, Python, Go, Laravel, Rails

example_repos.name: PatrickJS/awesome-cursorrules
example_repos.notes: The main curated list. Hundreds of examples organized by technology.

copilot_instructions.description: GitHub Copilot custom instructions file (.github/copilot-instructions.md) that guides Copilot across chat, code review, and editing.
recommended_content: Summary of what the app does
key_patterns: Use distinct headings and bullet points
Short imperative directives, not long narratives
Include reasoning behind rules (helps edge cases)
Use code examples for preferred/avoided patterns

example_repos.name: SebastienDegodez/copilot-instructions

amplified_dev.description: A philosophical manifesto by Continue about the future of developer work with AI. Not a technical spec but a community statement: 'A way of working where AI handles the volume and you handle the signal.'
amplified_dev.key_thesis: Developer roles expand (not shrink) as each layer becomes automated. AI is the next layer.

aicodingrules_org.description: Proposed vendor-agnostic standard for AI coding agent rules. Combines YAML metadata + Markdown guidance.
aicodingrules_org.hierarchy: Organization Rules > User Global Rules > User Project/Workspace Rules

continuedev_awesome_rules.description: Community collection of markdown rules with YAML frontmatter, compatible across AI coding assistants.

rules_cli.description: CLI for managing rules across any AI IDE

google_styleguide.description: Copies of Google's internal style guides for open-source projects. Covers C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, Shell, Objective-C, XML, HTML/CSS.
google_styleguide.structure: Separate guide per language, hosted via gh-pages at google.github.io/styleguide
google_styleguide.contribution_policy: External contributions NOT accepted. Internal-first process.
google_styleguide.key_insight: Very prescriptive. Each guide covers naming, formatting, commenting, imports, and language-specific patterns in exhaustive detail.

airbnb_javascript.description: One of the most popular JavaScript style guides. Covers types, references, objects, arrays, destructuring, strings, functions, classes, modules, iterators, properties, variables, hoisting, comparison, blocks, comments, whitespace, commas, semicolons, type casting, naming, accessors, events, testing.
airbnb_javascript.structure: Single massive README with numbered rules, each with code examples (good/bad).
airbnb_javascript.key_insight: Encourages forking and customizing. Available in 30+ languages.

python_pep8.description: The definitive Python style guide. Covers indentation, maximum line length, blank lines, imports, module-level dunder names, string quotes, whitespace, trailing commas, comments, naming conventions.
python_pep8.enforcement: ruff, flake8, pycodestyle, autopep8, black, yapf

rust_style_guide.description: Official Rust style guide. 4-space indentation, 100-char line width.

recommended_sections: How to report bugs and suggest features

commit_message_conventions.format: Imperative mood, present tense ('Fix bug' not 'Fixed bug')
commit_message_conventions.body: 72 character wrap, explain what and why not how

contributing_md_best_practices.key_insight: Style guides and linters should be used to standardize contributions. Contributors should follow existing patterns for consistency.

project_guidelines_template.description: Comprehensive JavaScript project guidelines covering 11 areas
sections: 1. Git workflow (feature branches, interactive rebase, PRs)
5. Testing (file naming, pure functions, co-located tests)
6. Project structure (organize by feature not role)
8. Logging (no console.logs in production, use libraries)
project_guidelines_template.key_insight: Organize by feature (product/, user/) not by role (controllers/, models/). Use lint-staged + Husky for pre-commit hooks.

section_3_architecture_decision_records.title: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
section_3_architecture_decision_records.summary: ADRs capture important architectural decisions with context and consequences. Multiple templates and tools exist.

key_repos.name: joelparkerhenderson/architecture-decision-record
key_repos.description: Comprehensive ADR resource with templates, examples, and best practices.

key_repos.name: npryce/adr-tools
key_repos.description: Command-line tools for working with ADRs as Markdown files.

key_repos.name: adr/madr
key_repos.description: Markdown Architectural Decision Records (MADR) - emphasizes options and pros/cons.

key_repos.name: thomvaill/log4brains
key_repos.description: ADR management and publication tool - generates static website from ADR files.

key_repos.name: zircote/git-adr
key_repos.description: ADRs stored in git notes (no files, no merge conflicts). AI-powered drafting.

templates: Jeff Tyree and Art Akerman's Template (more sophisticated)
best_practices: Keep each record focused on one decision
Add timestamps to track when recorded
Maintain immutability or clearly mark amendments
Use present-tense imperative verbs in filenames (choose-database.md)
Store in adr/ directory, commit to version control
Plan after-action reviews (typically one month later)
Reference subsequent ADRs triggered by decisions
section_3_architecture_decision_records.lifecycle: Initiating > Researching > Evaluating > Implementing > Maintaining > Sunsetting

section_4_project_structure_conventions.title: Project Structure Conventions
section_4_project_structure_conventions.summary: Common patterns for organizing code in repositories, with emphasis on Python monorepos and feature-based organization.

common_structures.name: Libs and Apps Split
common_structures.description: Split packages into libs (importable, no entry points) and apps (runnable services)

common_structures.name: Src-layout with namespace packages
common_structures.description: Each project has src/, tests/, pyproject.toml. Namespace packages for shared hierarchy.

common_structures.name: Top-level categorization
common_structures.description: Two top-level folders: one for projects, one for shared libraries.

best_practices: Each project has its own pyproject.toml
All packages installed in editable mode
Use uv, poetry, or pip for dependency management

organize_by_feature_not_role.description: Instead of controllers/, models/, views/, use product/, user/, auth/ each containing their own code, tests, and config.
organize_by_feature_not_role.benefits: Easier navigation, encapsulated modules, clearer dependencies

standard_config_files.purpose: Standardizes editor behavior (encoding, indentation, line endings) across teams
Prevents unwanted files from being committed
Controls line ending normalization, diff/merge drivers, language detection

section_5_developer_experience_and_workf.title: Developer Experience & Workflow Automation
section_5_developer_experience_and_workf.summary: DX tools and practices focus on reducing friction, automating quality checks, and streamlining development workflows.

trunk_based_development.description: Developers commit to main branch multiple times a day with small, incremental updates.
key_practices: Feature flags instead of long-lived branches
Keep number of active branches minimal
trunk_based_development.benefits: Quick feedback loops, fewer merge conflicts, continuously releasable state
trunk_based_development.ci_integration: Every push triggers automated tests, builds, security scans

git_flow.description: Feature branches, develop branch, release branches, hotfixes

github_flow.description: Main branch + feature branches + pull requests

section_6_ai_coding_workflows.title: AI Coding Workflows and Tools
section_6_ai_coding_workflows.summary: Multiple paradigms have emerged for AI-assisted development: spec-driven development, agentic workflows, and context engineering.

spec_driven_development.description: Methodology where formal specifications serve as executable blueprints for AI code generation.
spec_driven_development.workflow: Constitution > Specify > Clarify > Plan > Tasks > Implement
spec_driven_development.supported_agents: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini, 16+ total
spec_driven_development.key_insight: Most powerful for adding features to existing codebases. Forces clarity on system interactions.

github_agentic_workflows.description: Write workflows in plain Markdown in .github/workflows/. AI handles decision-making for issue triage, PR reviews, CI failure analysis.
key_features: Preapproved safe outputs for write operations
Supports Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot

context_engineering.description: The discipline of curating what the model sees to optimize desired outcomes. The most important factor in AI coding agent effectiveness.

key_principles: Treat context as finite with diminishing returns
Find the smallest set of high-signal tokens that maximize desired outcomes
System prompts: specific enough to guide, flexible enough for heuristics
Start minimal, add instructions based on failure modes
techniques: System prompt design (XML tags, Markdown headers, distinct sections)
Just-in-time context retrieval (lightweight identifiers, dynamic loading)
Structured note-taking (persistent notes outside context window)

context_engineering.key_insight: Context files over a few thousand tokens cause critical rules to get lost in the middle. Context engineering is the most important skill for AI-assisted development.

section_7_company_practices.title: How Companies Document Standards
section_7_company_practices.summary: Most large companies keep internal standards proprietary, but some patterns are visible through public artifacts and blog posts.

stripe.approach: Specification-first development. Every API endpoint begins with comprehensive OpenAPI documentation.
stripe.observability: Writes metrics to both old and new services simultaneously during migrations. Internal documentation, office hours, and internal champions.

google.approach: Exhaustive internal style guides that are periodically published as open source (google/styleguide). Internal-first: external contributions not accepted.
google.covers: C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, Shell, Objective-C, XML, HTML/CSS, Go

python_cpython.approach: Comprehensive developer guide (devguide.python.org). PEP 8 style guide. PEP process for proposals.
python_cpython.key_insight: Separate devguide site rather than in-repo CONTRIBUTING.md. Checklist-based contribution process.

rust_lang.approach: Official style guide enforced by rustfmt. rustc-dev-guide for compiler contributors.

section_7_company_practices.key_insight: The most effective standards are enforced by tooling (linters, formatters, CI checks), not just documentation.

section_8_key_patterns_and_templates.title: Reusable Patterns and Templates
section_8_key_patterns_and_templates.summary: Cross-cutting patterns that appear across all sources.
what_makes_good_coding_standards_docs: Concise and scannable (headings, bullet points, tables)
Code examples for every rule (good AND bad patterns)
Version controlled and treated as living documents
Iterated based on actual mistakes (not theoretical)
Progressive disclosure (core rules first, details on demand)
Machine-readable where possible (for AI agents and linters)
universal_sections_for_any_project: Git workflow (branching, commit messages, PR process)
ai_instruction_file_common_patterns: Code style preferences that differ from defaults
emerging_trends_2025_2026: AI instruction files becoming standard project artifacts
Context engineering as a core developer skill
Unified rule standards across AI tools (aicodingrules.org)
Deterministic hooks for guaranteed actions vs advisory rules
